thread:
Alex: FYI PR 6734 ready for merge but benchmark showed a small tail bump on long-seq workloads. tagging for reviews. https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6734 :eyes:
Maria: Can you paste the bench outputs? what workload and seed?
Alex: Ran local perf harness against canary image. workload = long-seq-32k, batch=8, kv_cache_enabled=true. Results: 50p/95p/99p latency (ms) before -> after: 22/120/215 -> 23/130/235. Throughput dropped ~4%. Small but consistent across runs.
Cheng: Can you share the exact command + log snippet? I can run on perf infra.
Alex: Command I used:
```
./perf/run_bench --workload long-seq-32k --batch 8 --replicas 4 --runs 5 --image redwood/canary:pr-6734
```
Log excerpt (one run):
```
[run 3] qps: 345.2, avg=24.1ms, p95=130.3ms, p99=235.6ms, mem_rss=12.1GB
```
Maria: Hmm p95/p99 delta is higher than I'd expect for that change. What diff landed in the PR?
Alex: It's a small tweak to KV eviction threshold and a race fix in the scheduler. Diff snippet:
```
- if (cache.size() > HARD_LIMIT) evict_oldest();
+ if (cache.size() > HARD_LIMIT && !is_inflight()) evict_oldest();
```
That guard was to reduce double-evict churn but could keep more stale entries.
Sam: Could be more cache hits but bigger KV arrays -> more memcpy on restore? did you see mem alloc spike?
Alex: mem_rss in logs hovered same; allocation profile didn't show big instantaneous allocs but CPU on restore path rose ~6%.
Hana: CI-bot shows the pre-merge canary smoke passed but perf tests are flaky: https://ci.redwood/flow/8921 :thumbsup:
CI-bot: canary-smoke: passed, unit-tests: passed, perf-regression-check: flaky (3/5 runs flagged).
Cheng: I can bisect the change by running perf on the two commits (pre/patch). Give me commit SHAs and I'll run on perf cluster tomorrow morning.
Alex: commits: a1f4c2b (base), d3e9f77 (PR). I'll hold the merge until we rule out regression.
Maria: For speed, can we run the same harness with `--prefill-cache` to check if warm cache changes tail? also try batch=16 to see batch sensitivity.
Sam: I'll spin a quick synthetic on my dev rig with batch=16 and prefill. ping me in ~30m.
Alex: Thanks. Also adding unit test for eviction guard. Will push extra asserts that simulate concurrent inflight ops.
Hana: Ping reviewers: @Maria @Cheng for approve once bisect/bench confirm. If a regression is confirmed, we should revert d3e9f77 and reintroduce with a safer fix.
Maria: Agreed. If bisect shows PR commit is culprit, revert + patch later. If it's noise, we can annotate canary and proceed.
Cheng: Ack — I'll run the cluster job and post raw logs here. planning to run 3 seeds and post aggregated p50/p95/p99 + CPU profile.
Sam: ran quick dev run with prefill and batch=16: p95 delta reduced to ~3% (125 -> 129ms) but p99 still up 6%. sending raw logs in 10m.
Alex: Appreciate the help. Holding merge until we have Cheng's cluster results.
Maria: Thanks Alex — please add a short blurb in PR description about the possible perf impact so reviewers notice.
Alex: done. PR updated with notes and links to these logs. :white_check_mark:
CI-bot: comment: "build a1f4c2b..d3e9f77: perf-suite queued on perf-cluster-02"
Cheng: posted results: aggregate across 3 seeds:
```
base a1f4c2b: p50=22.3ms, p95=121.0ms, p99=218.2ms, qps=358
pr d3e9f77: p50=23.1ms, p95=131.5ms, p99=245.9ms, qps=344
```
CPU flame shows longer restore path by ~8%. I think eviction guard keeps slightly older entries causing heavier restore cost.
Maria: thanks. Based on this let's revert on main and rework eviction logic. @Alex can you open a follow-up PR with revert + an issue describing approach?
Alex: Opening revert PR now and a redesign ticket for eviction policy that avoids keeping inflight-protected old entries. Will include perf tests.
Sam: lgtm. happy to help design/benchmark new policy.
Hana: OK moving to revert flow. tagging infra to schedule a controlled canary revert window tonight. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Alex: Thanks everyone — will follow up with PR links shortly.
